highlight.title: BGP Vortex: The New Internet Routing Vulnerability That Could Take Down 96% of Networks
highlight.summary: Researchers discovered BGP Vortex, a vulnerability that can flood the internet with routing messages and cause massive outages lasting up to 40 seconds. Just 21 of the world's largest networks are vulnerable, but triggering all identified vortices could impact nearly the entire internet.

resources.title: A Beginner's Guide To Computer Networking
resources.why_now: Perfect entry point explaining networks as 'roads between cities' with real-world analogies. Covers the fundamentals like TCP/IP, Wi-Fi vs Ethernet, and routing in digestible terms that make sense to complete beginners.

resources.title: What Happens When You Type a URL Into Your Browser?
resources.why_now: Updated March 2026 guide breaking down the entire journey from typing 'google.com' to seeing a webpage. Shows DNS lookups, TCP handshakes, and TLS encryption in action—the perfect real-world example of how all networking concepts work together.

resources.title: 8 Hot Networking Trends for 2026
resources.why_now: Network World's analysis of how AI is transforming networking operations, with autonomous systems handling Tier 1 and Tier 2 infrastructure tasks. Essential reading for understanding where enterprise networking is headed in the AI era.

resources.title: freeCodeCamp Free Computer Networking Course 2026
resources.why_now: Comprehensive free course covering TCP/IP fundamentals, subnetting, and VLSM with hands-on exercises. Perfect for anyone wanting to go beyond basics and gain practical networking skills without expensive certification programs.

claude_take: The internet feels magical until you realize it's held together by 30-year-old protocols like BGP that can crash spectacularly when misconfigured. Understanding how DNS turns google.com into an IP address, or why your Wi-Fi works, isn't just academic—it's essential digital literacy in a world where network outages can shut down entire services we depend on daily.
